This NetworkX change gives the agent one file. Each file retains its eight most recent co-edits. A commit can outlive one file's window because another participant still retains it.
Open the evidence list. The additional commits identify their retaining files. Here the test for the directed generator enters the top eight. These ranks use only earlier commits.
Now the agent knows two files from a Dask change. The local SQLite database computes three rankings from the same eight past events. The hidden files are used only to grade the result.
The sum of pair weights finds zero of three files. Giving extra weight to candidates present with both seeds finds two. A control using pair overlap alone finds all three.
Expand a commit to see the actual participants and its source revision. The same files and the same storage budget can give different next reads under different scoring rules.
Switch to a change in Xarray. The simple pair ranking finds one of two hidden files. Giving extra weight to joint events displaces it. The effect varies across real changes.
In this controlled example every pair from different file groups occurs exactly once. Select an A file and a B file. The highlighted C file is the recorded third participant.
Change the history. The highlighted file moves while all pair counts stay fixed. Across sixteen equally likely histories, an eight-file answer from those counts can cover at most half.

Stored events preserve information that pair counts can lose. On six new real repositories the additional information did not establish a consistent retrieval advantage. Both outcomes are available for inspection.
